setup.en: At an Albuquerque bus stop, a warehouse picker studies the crew’s walking route.
setup.es: En una parada de autobús de Albuquerque, una empleada de almacén estudia la ruta a pie del grupo.
setup.it: A una fermata dell’autobus di Albuquerque, un’addetta al magazzino studia il percorso a piedi del gruppo.
setup.ar: عند موقف حافلات في ألباكركي، تتفحّص عاملة مستودع مسار سير الفريق على الأقدام.

text.en: In September 2025, Albuquerque said Trump’s administration tried to withdraw $11.5 million for the Rail Trail while favoring car-based projects.
text.es: En septiembre de 2025, Albuquerque afirmó que la administración Trump intentó retirar 11,5 millones de dólares destinados al Rail Trail mientras favorecía proyectos para automóviles.
text.it: Nel settembre 2025, Albuquerque ha dichiarato che l’amministrazione Trump aveva tentato di ritirare 11,5 milioni di dollari destinati al Rail Trail, favorendo progetti per le automobili.
text.ar: في سبتمبر 2025، قالت ألباكركي إن إدارة ترامب حاولت سحب 11.5 مليون دولار مخصّصة لمسار ريل تريل، مع تفضيل مشاريع تعتمد على السيارات.

comment.en: “Trump wants projects for cars.” She points at your shoes. “Put a license plate on those. We might get you a sidewalk.”
comment.es: «Trump quiere proyectos para coches». Señala vuestros zapatos. «Ponedles una matrícula. A lo mejor conseguimos una acera».
comment.it: «Trump vuole progetti per le auto». Indica le vostre scarpe. «Metteteci una targa. Forse vi procuriamo un marciapiede».
comment.ar: «ترامب يريد مشاريع للسيارات». تشير إلى أحذيتكم. «ضعوا عليها لوحات أرقام. ربما نحصل لكم على رصيف».

sources.title: Trump Administration Attempts to Cancel Money for Rail Trail
sources.qualification: City account of an attempted $11.5 million cancellation; not a claim that the entire trail closed or the dispute ended.

notes.es: Versión municipal de un intento de cancelar 11,5 millones de dólares. No implica que cerrara todo el sendero ni que terminara la disputa.
notes.it: Resoconto comunale del tentativo di cancellare 11,5 milioni di dollari. Non indica la chiusura dell’intero percorso né la conclusione della controversia.
notes.ar: رواية البلدية عن محاولة إلغاء تمويل بقيمة 11.5 مليون دولار؛ لا تعني إغلاق المسار بأكمله أو انتهاء النزاع.

setup.en: Outside an Albuquerque laundromat, a retired machinist discusses the city’s lawsuit while the crew waits for dry clothes.
setup.es: Frente a una lavandería de Albuquerque, una mecánica industrial jubilada comenta la demanda municipal mientras el grupo espera a que se seque la ropa.
setup.it: Davanti a una lavanderia di Albuquerque, un’operaia meccanica in pensione parla della causa del Comune mentre il gruppo aspetta che i vestiti si asciughino.
setup.ar: أمام مغسلة في ألباكركي، تناقش عاملة تشغيل آلات متقاعدة دعوى البلدية بينما ينتظر الفريق جفاف الملابس.

text.en: In July 2025, Albuquerque challenged Trump’s immigration conditions on police grants supporting officer salaries, evidence processing and crime-victim services.
text.es: En julio de 2025, Albuquerque impugnó las condiciones migratorias de Trump sobre subvenciones policiales que financiaban salarios, procesamiento de pruebas y servicios a víctimas de delitos.
text.it: Nel luglio 2025, Albuquerque ha contestato le condizioni sull’immigrazione imposte da Trump ai finanziamenti per stipendi degli agenti, analisi delle prove e servizi alle vittime di reato.
text.ar: في يوليو 2025، طعنت ألباكركي في شروط ترامب المتعلقة بالهجرة على منح للشرطة تموّل رواتب الضباط ومعالجة الأدلة وخدمات ضحايا الجرائم.

comment.en: “Trump threatened police money over immigration. So when somebody steals my bike, should I report a theft or ask whether it crossed a border?”
comment.es: «Trump amenazó los fondos de la policía por la inmigración. Si alguien me roba la bici, ¿denuncio un robo o pregunto si cruzó una frontera?»
comment.it: «Trump ha minacciato i fondi della polizia per l’immigrazione. Se mi rubano la bici, denuncio un furto o chiedo se ha attraversato un confine?»
comment.ar: «ترامب هدّد تمويل الشرطة بسبب الهجرة. إذا سرق أحدهم دراجتي، هل أبلّغ عن سرقة أم أسأل إن كانت قد عبرت الحدود؟»

sources.title: City Joins Lawsuits to Block Federal Cuts to Public Safety, Housing
sources.qualification: City’s account of threatened grants and litigation; no claim that all funding was lost or services stopped.

notes.es: Versión municipal de las subvenciones amenazadas y el litigio. No afirma que se perdieran todos los fondos ni que se suspendieran los servicios.
notes.it: Resoconto comunale dei finanziamenti minacciati e della causa. Non afferma che tutti i fondi siano andati persi o che i servizi siano cessati.
notes.ar: رواية البلدية عن المنح المهدّدة والتقاضي؛ لا تفيد بخسارة التمويل كله أو توقف الخدمات.

setup.en: Outside an Albuquerque rental office, a grounds worker compares notices with the travelers.
setup.es: Frente a una oficina de alquileres de Albuquerque, una trabajadora de mantenimiento de jardines compara avisos con el grupo.
setup.it: Davanti a un ufficio affitti di Albuquerque, un’addetta alla manutenzione del verde confronta gli avvisi con il gruppo.
setup.ar: أمام مكتب تأجير في ألباكركي، تقارن عاملة صيانة حدائق الإشعارات مع أفراد الفريق.

text.en: Albuquerque’s July 2025 lawsuit challenged Trump administration conditions threatening housing grants that supported rental assistance, eviction prevention and rehousing.
text.es: La demanda de Albuquerque de julio de 2025 impugnó condiciones de la administración Trump que amenazaban subvenciones de vivienda destinadas a ayudas al alquiler, prevención de desahucios y realojamiento.
text.it: La causa avviata da Albuquerque nel luglio 2025 contestava condizioni dell’amministrazione Trump che minacciavano fondi per contributi all’affitto, prevenzione degli sfratti e ricollocamento abitativo.
text.ar: طعنت دعوى ألباكركي في يوليو 2025 في شروط لإدارة ترامب تهدّد منحاً سكنية تدعم المساعدة في الإيجار ومنع الإخلاء وإعادة الإسكان.

comment.en: “Immigration conditions on housing money. I rent a one-bedroom. Apparently it needs a foreign policy.”
comment.es: «Condiciones migratorias para el dinero de vivienda. Alquilo un piso de un dormitorio. Por lo visto necesita política exterior».
comment.it: «Condizioni sull’immigrazione per i fondi abitativi. Affitto un bilocale. A quanto pare gli serve una politica estera».
comment.ar: «شروط هجرة على تمويل السكن. أستأجر شقة بغرفة نوم واحدة. يبدو أنها تحتاج إلى سياسة خارجية».

sources.title: City Joins Lawsuits to Block Federal Cuts to Public Safety, Housing
sources.qualification: City’s account of threatened grants and litigation; no claim that all funding was lost or services stopped.

notes.es: Versión municipal de las subvenciones amenazadas y el litigio. No afirma que se perdieran todos los fondos ni que se suspendieran los servicios.
notes.it: Resoconto comunale dei finanziamenti minacciati e della causa. Non afferma che tutti i fondi siano andati persi o che i servizi siano cessati.
notes.ar: رواية البلدية عن المنح المهدّدة والتقاضي؛ لا تفيد بخسارة التمويل كله أو توقف الخدمات.

title.es: América primero, la carne ya llegará
title.it: Prima l’America, poi forse la carne

setup.en: At an Amarillo grocery picnic table, a feed-store loader notices the crew dividing a sandwich.
setup.es: En una mesa de picnic de una tienda de alimentación de Amarillo, una empleada que carga sacos de pienso ve al grupo repartirse un sándwich.
setup.it: A un tavolo da picnic di un alimentari di Amarillo, un’addetta al carico di un negozio di mangimi nota il gruppo che divide un panino.
setup.ar: عند طاولة نزهة بجوار متجر بقالة في أماريلو، تلاحظ عاملة تحميل في متجر أعلاف أن الفريق يتقاسم شطيرة.

text.en: Texas Farm Bureau objected in October 2025 to Trump’s proposal for more Argentine beef imports, warning it could hurt Texas ranchers.
text.es: Texas Farm Bureau se opuso en octubre de 2025 a la propuesta de Trump de aumentar las importaciones de carne de vacuno argentina, advirtiendo que podría perjudicar a los ganaderos de Texas.
text.it: Nell’ottobre 2025, Texas Farm Bureau si è opposta alla proposta di Trump di aumentare le importazioni di carne bovina argentina, avvertendo dei possibili danni agli allevatori texani.
text.ar: اعترض اتحاد مزارعي تكساس في أكتوبر 2025 على اقتراح ترامب زيادة واردات لحوم الأبقار الأرجنتينية، محذّراً من احتمال الإضرار بمربّي الماشية في تكساس.

comment.en: “Trump’s cheaper-beef plan upset our ranchers.” He inspects his sandwich. “I’ll notify Argentina when the affordable bit arrives.”
comment.es: «El plan de Trump para abaratar la carne enfadó a nuestros ganaderos». Examina su sándwich. «Avisaré a Argentina cuando llegue la parte barata».
comment.it: «Il piano di Trump per abbassare il prezzo della carne ha fatto infuriare i nostri allevatori». Esamina il panino. «Avviserò l’Argentina quando arriverà la parte economica».
comment.ar: «خطة ترامب لخفض سعر اللحم أغضبت مربّي الماشية عندنا». تتفحّص الشطيرة. «سأبلغ الأرجنتين عندما يصل الجزء الرخيص».

sources.title: Suggestions to increase Argentinian beef imports harm Texas cattle ranchers
sources.qualification: Farm Bureau advocacy statement about a proposed import expansion; statewide relevance, not measured Amarillo job losses.

notes.es: Declaración de una organización agraria sobre una propuesta de ampliar las importaciones. Tiene relevancia estatal; no mide pérdidas de empleo en Amarillo.
notes.it: Dichiarazione di un’organizzazione agricola su un aumento proposto delle importazioni. Riguarda il Texas; non misura posti di lavoro persi ad Amarillo.
notes.ar: موقف لاتحاد زراعي من مقترح لزيادة الواردات؛ صلته على مستوى الولاية، وليس قياساً لوظائف فُقدت في أماريلو.

title.es: El reloj de fichar del Gobierno

setup.en: At an Amarillo diner counter, a delivery driver reads a Pantex audit beside the travelers.
setup.es: En la barra de un restaurante de Amarillo, una repartidora lee una auditoría de Pantex junto al grupo.
setup.it: Al bancone di una tavola calda di Amarillo, un’autista addetta alle consegne legge un audit su Pantex accanto al gruppo.
setup.ar: عند منضدة مطعم في أماريلو، تقرأ سائقة توصيل تقرير تدقيق عن بانتيكس بجوار الفريق.

text.en: A 2025 federal audit reported that Pantex contractor CNS had repaid $18.4 million in 2024 for billing the government for hours not worked.
text.es: Una auditoría federal de 2025 informó de que CNS, contratista de Pantex, había reembolsado 18,4 millones de dólares en 2024 por facturar al Gobierno horas no trabajadas.
text.it: Un audit federale del 2025 ha riferito che CNS, appaltatrice di Pantex, aveva restituito 18,4 milioni di dollari nel 2024 per ore fatturate al governo ma non lavorate.
text.ar: أفاد تدقيق اتحادي عام 2025 بأن شركة CNS المتعاقدة مع بانتيكس أعادت 18.4 مليون دولار في 2024 بسبب فوترة الحكومة عن ساعات لم تُعمل.

comment.en: “Eighteen million for hours nobody worked.” He looks at your job hunt. “We’ve been asking whether they’re hiring. Ask whether they’re billing.”
comment.es: «Dieciocho millones por horas que nadie trabajó». Mira vuestra búsqueda de empleo. «Preguntábamos si contratan. Preguntad si facturan».
comment.it: «Diciotto milioni per ore che nessuno ha lavorato». Guarda la vostra ricerca di impiego. «Chiedevamo se assumono. Chiedete se fatturano».
comment.ar: «ثمانية عشر مليوناً مقابل ساعات لم يعملها أحد». تنظر إلى بحثكم عن عمل. «كنا نسأل إن كانوا يوظّفون. اسألوا إن كانوا يصدرون فواتير».

sources.title: Audit: DOE-OIG-25-36
sources.qualification: DOE inspector general says CNS paid $18.4 million in a 2024 settlement for claimed hours not worked; report also records operational harm and corrective controls.

notes.es: La inspección general del Departamento de Energía sitúa el pago de 18,4 millones en un acuerdo de 2024 por horas facturadas y no trabajadas. El informe también recoge perjuicios operativos y controles correctivos.
notes.it: L’ispettorato generale del Dipartimento dell’Energia attribuisce il pagamento di 18,4 milioni a un accordo del 2024 per ore dichiarate ma non lavorate. Il rapporto documenta anche danni operativi e controlli correttivi.
notes.ar: يذكر المفتش العام لوزارة الطاقة دفع CNS مبلغ 18.4 مليون دولار في تسوية عام 2024 عن ساعات مُطالَب بها لم تُعمل. ويسجّل التقرير أيضاً أضراراً تشغيلية وضوابط تصحيحية.

setup.en: While the van cools in Amarillo, an appliance repairer recalls the nuclear-worker firings.
setup.es: Mientras se enfría la furgoneta en Amarillo, una reparadora de electrodomésticos recuerda los despidos del personal nuclear.
setup.it: Mentre il furgone si raffredda ad Amarillo, una riparatrice di elettrodomestici ricorda i licenziamenti del personale nucleare.
setup.ar: بينما تبرد الشاحنة في أماريلو، تستعيد مصلّحة أجهزة منزلية خبر تسريح العاملين في المجال النووي.

text.en: In February 2025, Trump’s administration reversed most NNSA firings; AP reported Pantex near Amarillo among the hardest-hit offices in the DOGE cuts.
text.es: En febrero de 2025, la administración Trump revirtió la mayoría de los despidos de la NNSA. AP situó Pantex, cerca de Amarillo, entre las oficinas más afectadas por los recortes de DOGE.
text.it: Nel febbraio 2025, l’amministrazione Trump ha revocato la maggior parte dei licenziamenti della NNSA. AP ha indicato Pantex, vicino ad Amarillo, tra gli uffici più colpiti dai tagli di DOGE.
text.ar: في فبراير 2025، تراجعت إدارة ترامب عن معظم عمليات الفصل في الإدارة الوطنية للأمن النووي. وذكرت أسوشيتد برس أن بانتيكس قرب أماريلو كانت من أكثر المكاتب تضرراً من تخفيضات DOGE.

comment.en: “Fire the nuclear staff. Rehire the nuclear staff.” He points at your ignition. “Government efficiency: have we tried turning the country off and on?”
comment.es: «Despedir al personal nuclear. Volver a contratarlo». Señala el contacto. «Eficiencia gubernamental: ¿hemos probado a apagar y encender el país?»
comment.it: «Licenziare il personale nucleare. Riassumere il personale nucleare». Indica l’accensione. «Efficienza governativa: abbiamo provato a spegnere e riaccendere il Paese?»
comment.ar: «افصلوا الطاقم النووي. أعيدوا توظيف الطاقم النووي». تشير إلى مفتاح التشغيل. «كفاءة حكومية: هل جرّبنا إطفاء البلاد وإعادة تشغيلها؟»

sources.title: Trump administration tries to bring back fired nuclear weapons workers in DOGE reversal
sources.qualification: AP reported Pantex among the hardest-hit NNSA offices; most firings were reversed. Administration and AP sources disputed exact numbers, so none are used.

notes.es: AP situó Pantex entre las oficinas de la NNSA más afectadas; la mayoría de los despidos se revirtieron. La administración y las fuentes de AP discrepaban sobre las cifras exactas, por lo que aquí no se incluyen.
notes.it: AP ha indicato Pantex tra gli uffici NNSA più colpiti; la maggior parte dei licenziamenti è stata revocata. L’amministrazione e le fonti di AP contestavano le cifre esatte, qui non riportate.
notes.ar: ذكرت أسوشيتد برس بانتيكس ضمن أكثر مكاتب الإدارة الوطنية للأمن النووي تضرراً؛ وأُلغي معظم الفصل. اختلفت الإدارة ومصادر الوكالة على الأعداد الدقيقة، لذلك لا تُذكر هنا.

setup.en: Outside an Austin library, a retired delivery driver tells the travelers why a veterans’ reading group paused.

text.en: Austin-based Humanities Texas said its veterans’ reading program remained paused in May 2025 after the federal government terminated its operating grant on April 2.

comment.en: “The federal grant vanished. Veterans can still appear in campaign ads; apparently letting them discuss a book is where Washington draws the line.”

sources.title: Humanities Texas: From the Director, May 2025
sources.qualification: Organization self-report from May 2025; program statuses are historical, not asserted current.

setup.en: At an Austin discount store, a teacher compares classroom supplies with the travelers’ grocery money.

text.en: In 2025, Texas enacted Senate Bill 2 and allocated $1 billion to education accounts that can pay for private schooling.

comment.en: “Texas found a billion for education accounts that cover private school. I’m buying classroom pencils. Should I put an admissions office on the pencil cup?”

sources.title: Texas Education Freedom Accounts
sources.qualification: Official program says the 2025 Legislature appropriated $1 billion; private-school support is not a claim that public schools received no new funding.

setup.en: While you check an Austin parking meter, a bakery worker points from its timer to her ticket.

text.en: Austin’s council set the unpaid-meter fine at $75, effective March 1, 2025.

comment.en: “Seventy-five dollars if the meter expires. I’m feeding it before I buy lunch. Austin has taught a pole to eat first.”

sources.title: Austin council document setting the unpaid-meter fine
sources.qualification: The $75 figure applies to the unpaid-meter fine from March 1, 2025; it is not a universal parking penalty.

setup.en: At a Billings supermarket, a shelf stocker compares a protein bar with a pastry beside the travelers.

text.en: In May 2026, Montana announced federal approval for SNAP restrictions covering candy and prepared desserts while protecting protein bars and fresh baked goods.

comment.en: “USDA approved Montana’s food ban, with exceptions for protein bars and fresh baked goods. Hunger is simple. Your snack now needs a classification hearing.”

sources.title: USDA Approves Montana SNAP Food-Restriction Waiver
sources.qualification: State announcement of federal waiver approval; does not establish implementation date or measured health effects.

setup.en: Outside a Billings apartment building, a cleaner checks a state tax notice while the travelers ask directions.

text.en: Montana’s 2026 property-tax changes give qualifying primary residences and long-term rental properties a reduced rate, including eligible properties in Billings.

comment.en: “Montana’s tax break includes long-term rental properties. My landlord gets the relief. I’m hoping he lets me look at it during the next inspection.”

sources.title: 2026 Tax Information for Montana Property Owners
sources.qualification: State rules offer reduced rates for qualifying primary homes and long-term rentals; no guaranteed rent reduction is asserted.

setup.en: Near a Billings public building, a seamstress waits beside the travelers with some mending.

text.en: Montana’s 2025 House Bill 819 restricted which flags could be displayed on government property, including public schools and state buildings.

comment.en: “Montana’s lawmakers restricted the flags government can fly. My sewing machine has more settings than the state’s idea of freedom.”

sources.title: Montana House Bill 819, 2025
sources.qualification: Enacted legislation restricts flags displayed on government property; satire concerns government control of official displays, not private possession.

setup.en: At a Boise laundromat, a university mailroom worker reads an old funding update beside the travelers.

text.en: On January 30, 2025, Boise State said the Trump administration’s funding-freeze memo was withdrawn, while other executive orders still required reviews of affected awards.

comment.en: “Trump’s funding freeze was withdrawn, but the other orders still needed checking. Washington canceled the padlock and left the chain.”

sources.title: Boise State: Federal Funding Update, January 30, 2025
sources.qualification: Dated university guidance: withdrawal of one memo did not withdraw the other executive orders; no specific award loss asserted.

setup.en: Outside Boise City Hall, a delivery rider tells the travelers about the 2025 flag dispute.

text.en: In May 2025, Boise made the Pride flag an official city flag after Idaho restricted government flag displays.

comment.en: “Idaho restricted flags, so Boise made Pride official. The rainbow had to get a government job before the state would let it be seen.”

sources.title: Salt Lake City and Boise make pride flags official city emblems, skirting flag ban laws
sources.qualification: Describes the May 2025 response; does not claim the flag remained flying after later laws.

setup.en: At a Boise grocery store, a classroom aide compares fundraiser cookies with the travelers’ cheap lunch.

text.en: In February 2025, Idaho Governor Brad Little signed House Bill 93, creating a $50 million Parental Choice Tax Credit program.

comment.en: “Governor Little found fifty million for school-choice tax credits. Our fundraiser has oatmeal raisin. Clearly we hired the wrong lobbyist.”

sources.title: Gov. Little signs House Bill 93 creating the Parental Choice Tax Credit program
sources.qualification: Governor announces a $50 million program; no claim that public-school funding was eliminated.

setup.en: At a Cheyenne hardware store, a roofer discusses a state press release with the travelers.

text.en: In July 2025, Wyoming Secretary of State Chuck Gray praised Trump’s order ending wind and solar subsidies while championing coal, oil and gas.

comment.en: “Gray cheered Trump for ending wind and solar subsidies, then cheered coal and oil. A free market, with the secretary of state holding the scorecards.”

sources.title: Wyoming Secretary of State Praises Order to End Wind and Solar Subsidies
sources.qualification: Official political statement; accurately attributed advocacy, not proof of its economic claims.

title.en: Please Introduce Yourself to Your Government

setup.en: At a Cheyenne copy shop, a shift worker waits beside the travelers with some registration paperwork.

text.en: In March 2025, Wyoming enacted House Bill 156 requiring proof of U.S. citizenship and residency for voter registration; Secretary of State Chuck Gray celebrated it.

comment.en: “Gray wanted more proof of citizenship and residency. The government I’ve paid for all these years would like an introduction. Should I bring flowers?”

sources.title: Secretary Gray Celebrates Proof-of-Citizenship and Residency Voting Law
sources.qualification: State announcement of HB 156 becoming law; not instructions for current registration or a claim that lawful citizens were all rejected.

title.en: The State Has a Roofing Budget

setup.en: Near Wyoming’s Capitol, a roofer shares a lunch bench with the travelers.

text.en: Wyoming’s government repaired its Capitol dome and applied gold leaf imported from Italy during the restoration described in 2019.

comment.en: “The state covered its dome in Italian gold. I patch my roof with tar. The difference, apparently, is which one of us writes the budget.”

sources.title: A History of the Wyoming Capitol
sources.qualification: Wyoming State Historical Society account drawing on archives; suffrage statement does not claim universal enfranchisement irrespective of other eligibility barriers.

setup.en: At a Chicago station entrance, a hotel cleaner compares train routes with the travelers.

text.en: CTA sued Trump’s federal transportation agencies in March 2026 over money paused for its Red Line Extension and Red and Purple Modernization projects.

comment.en: “Trump’s agencies paused the train money. CTA sued. Apparently the Red Line needs a transfer through federal court before it can reach another neighborhood.”

sources.title: CTA Sues Over Paused Red Line Extension and Modernization Funding
sources.qualification: Transit agency account and litigation position; describes events through publication, not final court disposition.

setup.en: At a Chicago corner store, a delivery driver discusses Trump’s attempted Guard deployment with the travelers.

text.en: In December 2025, the Supreme Court kept Trump’s attempted National Guard deployment to the Chicago area blocked while litigation continued.

comment.en: “Trump tried to send troops; the courts said wait. I can’t park here without permission, but the president thought the whole city was his loading zone.”

sources.title: Supreme Court keeps Trump’s National Guard deployment blocked in the Chicago area, for now
sources.qualification: Interim Supreme Court order, not a final merits ruling; no claim of a current troop deployment.

setup.en: At a Chicago bus stop, a grocery clerk counts change beside the travelers.

text.en: After Illinois passed a transit-funding bill, CTA approved its 2026 budget without fare increases, service cuts or layoffs.

comment.en: “Illinois passed transit funding, so CTA avoided the fare hike. Incredible technology: legislators release money and ordinary people get to keep some.”

sources.title: Chicago Transit Board Approves 2026 CTA Budget
sources.qualification: CTA credited passage of Illinois SB2111 for avoiding fare increases, service cuts and layoffs in its approved 2026 budget.

setup.en: Outside a Cleveland school, a lunchroom worker talks with the travelers during dismissal.

text.en: Representative Shontel Brown said Trump’s administration notified Cleveland schools that GEAR UP college-access funding would end September 30, 2025.

comment.en: “Trump’s administration cut GEAR UP, the program helping students toward college. The ladder is still available; Washington just repossessed the bottom rungs.”

sources.title: Brown Calls for Restoration of Terminated Ohio Education Grants
sources.qualification: Congressional statement; termination notice verified in indexed source text. It is not a current program-status determination.

setup.en: On a Cleveland riverwalk, a dock worker recalls the Cuyahoga fires as the travelers stop for water.

text.en: The Cuyahoga burned in Cleveland in 1969. Trump’s March 2025 history directive called for changes to federal historical presentations under his administration’s account of American greatness.

comment.en: “Trump wants federal history restored to greatness. Our river caught fire. Should the caption say American water was working twice as hard?”

sources.title: National Park Service: The 1969 Cuyahoga River Fire
sources.qualification: NPS distinguishes documented events from the myth that one fire alone created environmental legislation.

sources.title: White House history intervention
sources.qualification: March 2025 action directed interventions in Smithsonian/federal historical presentation. The administration calls this restoring truth; that phrase is its framing, not an objective finding.

setup.en: At a Cleveland riverside bench, a retired sewer worker shares lunch space with the travelers.

text.en: Before the famous 1969 river fire, Cleveland voters approved a $100 million bond issue in 1968 for sewer construction and water-treatment upgrades.

comment.en: “Cleveland voters approved the cleanup money before the famous river fire. A hundred million to keep water wet. Industry’s contribution had been making it flammable.”

sources.title: National Park Service: The 1969 Cuyahoga River Fire
sources.qualification: NPS distinguishes documented events from the myth that one fire alone created environmental legislation.

setup.en: At a Columbia laundromat, a restaurant dishwasher waits beside the travelers.

text.en: Governor Mike Kehoe signed legislation ending Missouri’s paid-sick-leave requirement in August 2025; Columbia employers could still choose to provide it.

comment.en: “Governor Kehoe ended Missouri’s paid-sick-leave requirement. My fever can still stay home. It just needs to find somebody else to pay the rent.”

sources.title: Governor Kehoe Signs Tax Cuts and Business Legislation
sources.qualification: Governor’s account of HB567 and HB594; provisions apply statewide, including Columbia. Advocacy claims of benefits are not adopted.

sources.title: When do employees stop earning paid sick time due to HB567?
sources.qualification: Labor Department says the state mandate ended August 28, 2025; employers may voluntarily retain paid leave.

setup.en: At a Columbia grocery checkout, a retail stocker talks with the travelers while waiting in line.

text.en: Missouri’s 2025 law retained the scheduled $15 minimum wage but removed automatic inflation adjustments, affecting covered workers in Columbia and across the state.

comment.en: “Kehoe kept the fifteen-dollar minimum but removed its inflation adjustment. Somebody tell the groceries. They don’t appear to have received the freeze notice.”

sources.title: Governor Kehoe Signs Tax Cuts and Business Legislation
sources.qualification: Governor’s account of HB567 and HB594; provisions apply statewide, including Columbia. Advocacy claims of benefits are not adopted.

setup.en: At a Columbia bus shelter, a janitor opens a pay envelope beside the travelers.

text.en: Governor Kehoe signed a 2025 Missouri law allowing individuals to deduct federally reported capital gains from state taxable income; it applies to eligible Columbia taxpayers.

comment.en: “Kehoe gave individual capital gains a state income-tax deduction. I clean floors for money. Apparently I should sell the building while someone else cleans it.”

sources.title: Governor Kehoe Signs Tax Cuts and Business Legislation
sources.qualification: Governor’s account of HB567 and HB594; provisions apply statewide, including Columbia. Advocacy claims of benefits are not adopted.

setup.en: Beside Cumberland’s canal, a maintenance worker talks with the travelers over lunch.

text.en: After national park firings under Trump in 2025, the C&O Canal separately reported five early retirements, including its only carpenter and arborist.

comment.en: “Trump cut park staff nationally. Here the only carpenter took early retirement. If that bench collapses, we’ll call it a successful transition to meadow.”

sources.title: WTOP: What Budget Cuts and Reduced Staffing Could Mean for the NPS
sources.qualification: Reported park-wide staffing decline from 70 to 65; departures were early retirements, not five stated dismissals in Cumberland.

sources.title: DOGE and national park staffing
sources.qualification: The administration fired about 1000 newly hired NPS staff in February 2025, including maintenance and cleaning roles. Do not present every later park closure as caused by those firings.

setup.en: At Cumberland’s canal terminus, a delivery driver compares the travelers’ map with the waterway.

text.en: The C&O Canal ended at Cumberland without reaching Ohio. Trump’s January 2025 order renamed the Gulf of Mexico for federal use, without moving its shores.

comment.en: “This canal never reached Ohio. Trump renamed the Gulf. Call your van Washington and you’re there. Still out of gas, but geographically victorious.”

sources.title: NPS: Canal Construction
sources.qualification: Canal-wide history with Cumberland as its actual western terminus.

sources.title: Gulf renaming
sources.qualification: January 2025 EO directed federal use of Gulf of America and restoration of Mount McKinley naming; it did not change geography or claim universal international recognition.

setup.en: At a Cumberland supermarket, a home-care aide discusses Maryland’s leave timetable with the travelers.

text.en: Maryland’s October 2025 guidance put its new family-and-medical-leave benefits, including for eligible Cumberland workers, on a timetable beginning by January 3, 2028.

comment.en: “Maryland’s new paid family leave starts in 2028. I’ll tell my mother to schedule her recovery around the government’s recovery from scheduling.”

sources.title: Maryland FAMLI Frequently Asked Questions
sources.qualification: Official October 2025 program timetable sets benefits to start by January 3, 2028; other leave rights and existing employer benefits are separate.

setup.en: Outside a Dallas medical campus, a lab cleaner shares a shaded lunch table.

text.en: In February 2025, Dallas’s UT Southwestern warned that the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap could cost it more than $100 million a year.

comment.en: “They call freezers overhead. Let a senator keep his lunch at room temperature and see how fast overhead becomes critical infrastructure.”

sources.title: Proposed NIH overhead cap
sources.qualification: UT Southwestern estimated in February 2025 that the proposed cap risked over 100m yearly. Do not present the estimate or proposal as an already realized local loss.

setup.en: At a Dallas laundromat, a renter compares housing costs while the van blankets dry.

text.en: Texas law exempts $140,000 of a qualifying residence homestead’s value from school taxes. The applicant must own an interest in the home and live there.

comment.en: “Texas has tax relief for your home. First, own one. I checked: my security deposit does not count as a down payment on freedom.”

sources.title: Texas Comptroller: Property Tax Exemptions
sources.qualification: Current exemption and ownership criteria checked September 2026; no claim that tenants receive this exemption or automatic rent savings.

setup.en: Near Fair Park, a custodian chats with you during a food break.

text.en: Dallas’s federally funded Hall of Negro Life opened in 1936 and was demolished in 1937. In March 2025, Trump ordered changes to federal presentations of American history.

comment.en: “The federal Black history hall here was demolished in 1937. Now Trump wants history corrected. I would bolt the exhibit to the floor.”

sources.title: City of Dallas: The 1936 Hall of Negro Life
sources.qualification: The federally funded hall opened in 1936 and was deconstructed one year later. This historical event is separate from the 2025 order.

sources.title: White House history intervention
sources.qualification: The 2025 order directed interventions in federal historical presentation. The resident and proposed bolts are fictional.

setup.en: At a Denver bus shelter, a kitchen worker tells you about the city’s unpaid federal bill.

text.en: In April 2025, FEMA denied Denver about $24 million in reimbursement for migrant services the city had already provided.

comment.en: “Washington said help the arrivals, then refused the reimbursement. I tried that with my landlord: patriotic housing partnership. He still wants the rent.”

sources.title: Denverite: What Losing $24M of Federal Money Really Means for Denver
sources.qualification: Dated report of canceled reimbursements for prior spending; not a claim about the ultimate dispute outcome.

setup.en: Over food outside a Denver grocery, a warehouse worker explains Colorado’s extra union ballot.

text.en: In May 2025, Governor Jared Polis vetoed a bill removing Colorado’s second-election requirement for negotiating a union-security agreement.

comment.en: “Polis kept the second vote for a union security agreement. Funny: when the boss announces a pay freeze, we never get a first vote.”

sources.title: Colorado General Assembly: SB25-005 Worker Protection Collective Bargaining
sources.qualification: Vetoed bill; the extra election concerns union-security agreements, not whether workers may form a union.

setup.en: Near the Denver Mint, a grocery clerk compares the coins in your palms.

text.en: Trump ordered an end to circulating penny production in 2025. Denver had made the coins; existing pennies remain legal tender.

comment.en: “Trump stopped making pennies. The price tags still end in ninety-nine. Apparently the smallest government service was giving me my change.”

sources.title: AP: US Mint presses final pennies as production ends
sources.qualification: Production ended, not legal-tender status; final public ceremony was in Philadelphia, not Denver.

sources.title: US Mint: Penny
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: At a Des Moines produce stall, a delivery worker points to the unsold apples.

text.en: In 2025, Trump’s USDA ended two Iowa local-food purchasing programs. One orchard needed new buyers for 50,000 pounds of apples.

comment.en: “Trump’s USDA canceled the local-food programs. The apples still passed inspection. Unfortunately, they failed the new test: being lunch for someone who needs it.”

sources.title: Radio Iowa: Farmers Feel the Impact of Local Food Programs Being Eliminated
sources.qualification: Statewide program cancellation applicable to Iowa; no unverified Des Moines-specific tonnage, school closure or job loss.

setup.en: At a Des Moines laundromat, a bus driver holds an electric bill up to the window beside your folding table.

text.en: Des Moines’s electric franchise fee rose to 7.5% in 2025.

comment.en: “City gets seven and a half percent when I turn on a lamp. I read the bill by the window now. The sun hasn’t signed a franchise agreement.”

sources.title: Des Moines electric-franchise ordinance 16,485
sources.qualification: The ordinance establishes the 7.5% franchise-fee rate. No claim about an individual bill’s total increase or the electric utility’s underlying rates.

setup.en: At a Des Moines grocery exit, a school cook pauses beside your modest food purchase.

text.en: Starting in the 2025–26 school year, Iowa removed income limits for its state-funded education savings accounts for accredited private-school expenses.

comment.en: “Iowa’s private-school accounts no longer have an income ceiling. Finally, a billionaire can get tuition help without the indignity of needing it.”

sources.title: Iowa Department of Education: Students First Education Savings Accounts
sources.qualification: Universal income eligibility began in 2025–26; other residency, enrollment and application requirements remain.

setup.en: At an El Paso streetcar stop, a grocery clerk watches a visitor hunt through a wallet beside you.

text.en: El Paso’s Sun Metro streetcar is fare-free.

comment.en: “City streetcar’s free. You can tell who’s new: they board with their card out, like they’re feeding a nervous horse.”

sources.title: Sun Metro: About the Streetcars
sources.qualification: Fare-free service applies to the streetcar; no claim about other bus fares, service frequency or reliability.

setup.en: While you ask about a charging cable, an El Paso repair-shop owner holds a necktie against a refrigerator.

text.en: El Paso’s December 2023 Meta agreement offered an 80% city property-tax rebate for its first phase, conditioned on $800 million investment and 50 jobs.

comment.en: “Meta can get eighty percent of its city property tax back. I’m putting a tie on the fridge. One of us is going to qualify.”

sources.title: City of El Paso: Data Centers
sources.qualification: First-phase city property-tax rebate: 80%, 15 years, with stated investment and job conditions. No assertion of actual job delivery or exemption from school and county taxes.

setup.en: At an El Paso grocery exit, a stocker watches you total the cost of some supplies.

text.en: El Paso sits on the Mexican border. New York Fed researchers found US firms and consumers bore most of the cost of Trump’s 2025 tariffs.

comment.en: “Trump says foreigners pay his tariffs. I tried handing my grocery bill across the bridge. They handed it back. Excellent border security.”

sources.title: Trump tariffs passed to Americans
sources.qualification: 2026 New York Fed analysis finds most of the economic burden of 2025 tariffs fell on US firms and consumers. Fictional prices and shops are invented.

sources.title: National Park Service: Chamizal History and Culture
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: At a Flagstaff picnic table, a plumber hears you discussing water for the next stretch.

text.en: Trump’s 2025 budget proposal would close Flagstaff’s Grand Canyon Monitoring and Research Center, threatening research used to manage the Colorado River and Glen Canyon Dam.

comment.en: “Trump proposed closing the canyon’s river-monitoring center. If I stopped checking leaks to save money, I would be called a former plumber.”

sources.title: KJZZ: Proposal Threatens Grand Canyon Monitoring and Research Center
sources.qualification: Reported proposed cuts and conditional closure risk; not a verified closure or realized local job loss.

setup.en: Outside a Flagstaff stargazing event, a mechanic steadies a battered amateur telescope.

text.en: Flagstaff’s Lowell Observatory discovered Pluto. Trump’s April 2026 budget proposal sought a 47% cut to NASA science; Congress would determine the actual funding.

comment.en: “Trump proposed cutting NASA science almost in half. We found Pluto with a telescope. His budget committee could lose it with a calculator.”

sources.title: American Astronomical Society: Policy Update, 8 April 2026
sources.qualification: Professional society analysis of a proposed FY2027 budget, not enacted cuts or a documented loss to Lowell.

sources.title: Lowell Observatory: This Week in Astronomy History, February 15–21
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: On a Flagstaff evening walk, a night cleaner stops where the stars show above the shops.

text.en: Flagstaff adopted an outdoor-lighting ordinance in 1958, using city regulation to protect the night sky for residents and observatories.

comment.en: “Flagstaff regulated outdoor lighting so we could see the stars. Terrible government interference. A billboard might have sold that sky something.”

sources.title: City of Flagstaff: Dark Sky
sources.qualification: City history of its 1958 ordinance and 2001 designation, not a current legal compliance guide.

setup.en: At a Frederick sandwich counter, a hospital porter discusses Trump’s announced federal health cuts.

text.en: Maryland’s March 31, 2025 layoff log listed ninety HHS positions in Frederick for elimination under Trump’s federal cuts, with a stated May 30 effective date.

comment.en: “Ninety health jobs marked for cuts. If I streamlined the hospital by removing the toilets, I would still have a mop problem.”

sources.title: Maryland Department of Labor: RIF Log Year 2025
sources.qualification: Formal notice lists 90 Frederick HHS positions and a May 30 effective date; notice is not an independent count of completed separations.

setup.en: At a Frederick laundromat, a cleaner compares rental applications while your clothes tumble.

text.en: Frederick County’s fair-housing rules protect source of income, including housing vouchers, limiting landlords’ ability to reject applicants simply because they use rental assistance.

comment.en: “The county says landlords cannot reject my housing voucher just for being a voucher. Government had to order them to accept government money. Very efficient market.”

sources.title: Frederick County: Housing Choice Voucher
sources.qualification: Source-of-income protection, not a guarantee of acceptance regardless of other lawful screening criteria.

setup.en: At a Frederick grocery bench, a care worker checks next month’s family calendar.

text.en: Maryland’s paid-family-leave program is scheduled to collect contributions from January 2027, with benefit payments beginning in January 2028.

comment.en: “Maryland’s paid-leave benefits start in 2028. I told Dad to reschedule his recovery. He asked whether the legislature also takes walk-ins.”

sources.title: Maryland Labor: Paid Family and Medical Leave Registration Is Live
sources.qualification: Contributions begin January 2027 and benefits January 2028; this is the scheduled rollout, not a currently payable benefit.

setup.en: Outside a Hagerstown post office, an off-duty carrier talks while you sort postcards.

text.en: Hagerstown postal workers announced a March 2025 anti-privatization rally after Trump and Musk discussed privatizing USPS; the proposal was not an enacted sale.

comment.en: “Trump and Musk floated privatizing the mail. Great: Grandma can become a premium delivery zone. She has always wanted to live inside a surcharge.”

sources.title: AP: Trump discusses privatizing the struggling Postal Service
sources.qualification: Proposal and political debate; no claim USPS was privatized or that a particular surcharge exists.

sources.title: Radio Free Hub City: Rally Against USPS Privatization
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: At a Hagerstown repair shop’s public bench, a bookkeeper waits with a stubborn laptop.

text.en: From July 1, 2025, Maryland imposed a 3% sales tax on specified data, information-technology and software-publishing services, adding to eligible service bills.

comment.en: “Maryland now taxes certain computer services. My laptop finally has a government job: every time it breaks, it raises revenue.”

sources.title: Maryland Comptroller: Technical Bulletin No. 56
sources.qualification: Tax covers specified service classifications, not every computer purchase or every repair.

setup.en: At a Hagerstown snack counter, a roofer checks stadium ticket prices while you study the menu.

text.en: Maryland’s 2021 law authorized bonds for Hagerstown’s new stadium; the state also committed supplemental and fiscal 2023 funding.

comment.en: “Public money helped build the ballpark. I asked about my seat. Apparently I paid for the building where they sell it to me again.”

sources.title: Maryland Stadium Authority: Groundbreaking for the downtown Hagerstown stadium
sources.qualification: Supports the state bond authority and identified public commitments. The resident’s seat exchange is invented; no claim of promised free admission or diversion from a named service.

setup.en: At an Iowa City café window, a dishwasher chats about the writing program’s lost grants.

text.en: In March 2025, State Department grant terminations ended several Iowa writing programs. The university said more than 90% of those federal grant dollars were spent in the US.

comment.en: “Trump’s State Department cut the writing program. More than ninety percent of its grant money stayed in America. Apparently America First has a spelling exception.”

sources.title: US Department of State halts International Writing Program funding
sources.qualification: University account of February 2025 grant termination and its announced effects; not a claim that every program ended permanently.

setup.en: Near the Iowa City campus, a cleaner points to an emptied office while taking a food break.

text.en: In March 2025, the University of Iowa announced its diversity division would close under state and regents directives; twelve jobs had been eliminated. Required civil-rights services continued elsewhere.

comment.en: “Iowa ordered the university to dismantle its diversity office. They removed twelve jobs in compliance. Equal opportunity now has equal opportunity to wait outside.”

sources.title: University of Iowa: Division Closure on March 27
sources.qualification: Twelve jobs eliminated since the previous spring, not twelve caused solely by this final closure; legally required services were reassigned.

setup.en: At an Iowa City bus shelter, a campus cleaner moves a lunchbox so you can sit.

text.en: Iowa City extended its fare-free bus pilot, as recorded in the city’s December 2025 strategic-plan progress report.

comment.en: “They extended the free-bus pilot. Still testing whether passengers miss paying. I’m willing to be observed keeping my money for as long as science needs.”

sources.title: Iowa City strategic-plan progress report, December 2025
sources.qualification: Supports extension of the fare-free pilot, not permanent funding or a claim that the program is an actual scientific experiment.

setup.en: At a Joplin hardware counter, a plumber holds a new drain fitting beside a sewer bill.

text.en: Joplin’s council approved sewer-rate increases beginning April 2025, averaging 4% annually through 2029; individual bills vary.

comment.en: “Council gave the sewer yearly increases through 2029. My boss says raises must be earned. The drain gets one just for swallowing.”

sources.title: Sewer rate adjustment begins for Joplin residents with April 2025 billing
sources.qualification: Average annual change over 2025–2029, with individual impacts varying. No claim about water safety, service failure or an exact household charge.

title.en: Stay Home on Your Own Time

setup.en: At a Joplin grocery exit, a cashier on break buys tissues beside your supplies.

text.en: Governor Mike Kehoe signed Missouri’s 2025 repeal of the voter-approved paid-sick-leave requirement, ending the state mandate on August 28.

comment.en: “Governor Kehoe repealed mandatory paid sick leave. The germs still clock in. Missouri protects your employer from catching the cost.”

sources.title: Governor Kehoe Signs Tax Cuts and Pro-Business Legislation
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: At a Joplin diner booth, a cleaner sorts pay slips beside a property-sale advertisement.

text.en: Missouri’s 2025 HB594 created a state income-tax deduction for individual capital gains. Ordinary wages, including a cleaner’s pay, do not become capital gains.

comment.en: “Missouri stopped taxing individuals’ capital gains. I clean expensive houses for taxable wages. My mop has been advised to diversify into owning the house.”

sources.title: Governor Kehoe Signs Tax Cuts and Pro-Business Legislation
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: Outside a Kansas City food pantry, a delivery worker discusses a canceled federal order.

text.en: In March 2025, Trump’s USDA canceled expected federal food shipments to Harvesters, serving Kansas and Missouri, including milk, eggs, cheese, chicken and fruit.

comment.en: “Trump’s USDA canceled food deliveries. The milk never arrived, but the savings did. Unfortunately, the children keep asking for the kind you can pour.”

sources.title: Trump administration cancels food bank shipments to Missouri and Kansas
sources.qualification: Regional reporting of Harvesters orders canceled in March 2025; no claim that all food-bank supplies stopped.

setup.en: At a Kansas City streetcar platform, a cook notices you searching for fare money.

text.en: Kansas City’s streetcar charges no fare. Its transportation district uses a sales tax and special property assessments to support the system’s construction and operation.

comment.en: “Local taxes pay for this ride. Put your wallet away. Yes, government did something useful. Try to look normal until we reach your stop.”

sources.title: KC Streetcar: Main Street Rail Transportation Development District
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

sources.title: KC Streetcar: About the Streetcar
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: At a Kansas City food counter, a cleaner in a plain baseball cap recalls the stadium vote.

text.en: Jackson County voters rejected an April 2024 proposal for forty years of sales taxes to help fund a new Royals ballpark and renovations to the Chiefs’ stadium.

comment.en: “They wanted forty years of sales taxes for stadiums. We voted no. For once, the fans got to send a billionaire back to the minors.”

sources.title: AP: Voters Reject Stadium Tax for Royals and Chiefs
sources.qualification: Dated failed ballot proposal; not a claim that subsequent stadium funding negotiations ended.

setup.en: At a La Crosse riverside bench, a bait-shop worker pauses beside your water jug.

text.en: A November 2025 report said Trump’s proposed federal budget could close La Crosse’s Upper Midwest Environmental Sciences Center. USGS emphasized that the budget had not passed.

comment.en: “Trump’s budget proposed closing our river science center. The fish cannot lobby. We are teaching one to hold a checkbook, but the ink runs.”

sources.title: Closure of Upper Midwest Environmental Sciences Center possible under proposed budget
sources.qualification: Local reporting of the proposed FY2026 budget; USGS said the budget had not passed. No completed closure is asserted.

setup.en: At a La Crosse copy shop, a school secretary holds a utility bill up to a pair of scissors.

text.en: Wisconsin’s Supreme Court upheld Governor Evers’s partial veto extending school revenue-limit increases through 2425. The ruling did not guarantee future appropriations.

comment.en: “Evers crossed out digits and got school revenue limits through 2425. I tried it on my electric bill. Apparently only one of us has constitutional scissors.”

sources.title: AP report on the upheld Wisconsin school revenue-limit veto
sources.qualification: The decision concerns revenue-limit increases through 2425, not an unconditional promise of 400 years of appropriations. The utility-bill comparison is invented satire.

setup.en: At a La Crosse grocery bench, a warehouse worker retrieves an ID from a worn wallet.

text.en: Wisconsin voters approved a legislatively proposed constitutional photo-ID requirement in April 2025. Photo ID was already required by state law.

comment.en: “We already showed photo ID. Legislators put it in the constitution. My terrible license photo now has stronger job security than I do.”

sources.title: AP: Wisconsin Voters Decide School Superintendent and Voter-ID Amendment
sources.qualification: The amendment entrenched a pre-existing photo-ID requirement; it did not introduce photo ID for the first time.

setup.en: At a Las Vegas bus stop, a hotel housekeeper watches an almost empty airport shuttle pass.

text.en: Las Vegas visitation fell 11% year over year in June 2025. Some officials cited Trump’s tariffs and immigration policies among possible causes; no single cause was established.

comment.en: “Trump wanted fewer foreigners coming in. Some tourists took the hint. My landlord has declined to accept a stronger border instead of rent.”

sources.title: Las Vegas tourism is down. Some blame Trump’s tariffs and immigration crackdown
sources.qualification: AP attributed part of the decline to officials and also reported other explanations; causation is not presented as settled.

setup.en: At a Las Vegas shaded water stop, a groundskeeper sets down a dusty rake.

text.en: Since November 2021, local rules have barred new golf courses in Las Vegas and unincorporated Clark County from using Colorado River water.

comment.en: “New golf courses cannot use Colorado River water. Finally, the government asked whether my drinking water really needs a putting lesson.”

sources.title: Drought and conservation measures
sources.qualification: Water district rules and water-use account checked September 2026; new-course restrictions differ from budgets for existing courses.

title.en: The Fine Print Leaves No Tip

setup.en: At a Las Vegas food court, an off-duty server checks a pay slip beside your lunch.

text.en: Trump’s 2025 law created a temporary income-tax deduction for eligible tips, with limits. It did not generally remove Social Security and Medicare taxes from those tips.

comment.en: “Trump promised no tax on tips. The deduction helps; payroll taxes still take a bite. Washington remains the customer who reads the menu and tips itself.”

sources.title: IRS: Tips
sources.qualification: Qualified-tip deduction has occupation, income, reporting and dollar limits and runs through 2028.

sources.title: IRS: Publication 15, Employer’s Tax Guide
sources.qualification: Reported tips remain generally subject to Social Security and Medicare taxes.

setup.en: At a Madison campus bus stop, a lab technician watches you check the van’s spare tire.

text.en: UW–Madison launched short-term bridge funding in May 2025 for research projects whose federal awards had been interrupted or terminated under Trump’s administration.

comment.en: “Trump interrupted research grants, so the university found bridge money. Science is driving on the spare while Washington takes credit for reducing tire expenses.”

sources.title: Building Bridges: Support for research impacted by federal funding cuts gets a boost from OVCR
sources.qualification: University account of bridge funding launched in May 2025 and additional initiatives; not a claim that all canceled funds were replaced.

setup.en: At a Madison diner, a cleaner describes the billionaire advertising in Wisconsin’s court race.

text.en: By March 30, 2025, Elon Musk and groups he supported had spent more than $20 million backing conservative Brad Schimel in Wisconsin’s Supreme Court election.

comment.en: “Musk brought millions to our Supreme Court election. I brought one vote. His came with surround sound; mine came with a pencil.”

sources.title: AP: Musk Gives Checks Ahead of Wisconsin Supreme Court Election
sources.qualification: Campaign support and outside spending, not bribery of a judge; amount is a dated minimum.

setup.en: At a Madison laundromat, a cook fishes an ID out of the clothes before washing.

text.en: In April 2025, Wisconsin voters approved the legislature’s amendment making photo ID a constitutional voting requirement, reinforcing the existing state-law rule.

comment.en: “Wisconsin put voter ID in the constitution. I nearly washed mine. Democracy now depends on whether I check my pockets before the spin cycle.”

sources.title: AP: Wisconsin Voters Decide School Superintendent and Voter-ID Amendment
sources.qualification: The amendment entrenched a pre-existing photo-ID requirement; it did not introduce photo ID for the first time.

setup.en: At a Minneapolis campus café patio, a lab cleaner shares a table with you.

text.en: By April 25, 2025, the University of Minnesota reported 72 terminated federal awards under Trump’s administration, affecting 220 personnel across the university.

comment.en: “Trump terminated research awards. Seventy-two of them. The university still studies uncertainty; Washington has simply moved the experiment into everyone’s paycheck.”

sources.title: Navigating Uncertainty: Research Leaders Update Board of Regents on Impact of Federal Funding Disruptions
sources.qualification: University-wide snapshot as of April 25, 2025; 220 personnel were affected, not necessarily laid off, and the total is not limited to Minneapolis.

setup.en: At a Minneapolis grocery bench, a delivery driver rocks a stroller while discussing leave.

text.en: Minnesota’s paid-family-and-medical-leave law, signed by Governor Tim Walz, established paid, job-protected leave for eligible workers beginning January 1, 2026.

comment.en: “Minnesota gives eligible workers paid family leave. My boss calls us a family too. Useful to discover which family pays when the baby arrives.”

sources.title: Governor Walz: Minnesota Paid Family Leave Begins January 2026
sources.qualification: Benefits and job protection have eligibility requirements; not every absence is covered.

setup.en: At a Minneapolis park table, a school cook eats after finishing the lunch shift.

text.en: Governor Walz signed Minnesota’s 2023 free-school-meals law, funding a breakfast and lunch at no charge for students at participating schools.

comment.en: “Walz made school meals free. Apparently six-year-olds should spend lunch chewing food instead of proving their parents are poor. Dangerous precedent for a government.”

sources.title: Minnesota Department of Education: Free School Meals for Kids
sources.qualification: Participating National School Lunch and School Breakfast Program schools; not every meal at every school.

title.en: The Freeze Has Thawed Into a Hold

setup.en: At a Missoula coffee counter, a university cleaner waits with a folded shift schedule.

text.en: On January 29, 2025, the University of Montana reported that Trump’s blanket federal funding freeze had been rescinded, while other reviews and communication pauses remained.

comment.en: “Trump withdrew the blanket funding freeze. Other reviews stayed. The fridge is open, the food is still locked up, and everyone applauds the thaw.”

sources.title: Federal funding freeze rescinded
sources.qualification: University notice verified through indexed text; direct page returned 404. Rescission did not cancel other orders or agency communication pauses.

setup.en: At a Missoula riverside rest, a maintenance worker points toward the Milltown area.

text.en: In a 2005 federal cleanup settlement, Atlantic Richfield and NorthWestern agreed to over $100 million in work at nearby Milltown Reservoir, including contaminated sediment removal and dam dismantling.

comment.en: “EPA made companies pay for the Milltown cleanup. The revolutionary principle of you broke it, you bought it finally reached a boardroom.”

sources.title: $100M settlement reached for Milltown Reservoir cleanup
sources.qualification: EPA announcement of the settlement and required cleanup near Missoula; no claim of a particular completion date.

title.en: The Car Can Fend for Itself

setup.en: At a Missoula yard sale, a carpenter shows you a sketch for a small backyard rental.

text.en: Missoula’s accessory-dwelling-unit code requires no additional parking for the added home.

comment.en: “A backyard home doesn’t need extra parking. I’ve drawn the tenant a kitchen. If the car wants its own living room, it can get a job.”

sources.title: Missoula municipal code, section 20.45.060: Accessory Dwelling Units
sources.qualification: Uses the current code rather than older planning PDFs. No claim of automatic permit approval or removal of every parking requirement.

setup.en: At a North Platte fuel stop, a farmhand checks the clouds while you fill the van.

text.en: In March 2025, amid Trump-era federal workforce cuts, staffing shortages reduced North Platte’s routine National Weather Service balloon launches from twice daily to once.

comment.en: “Trump’s cuts left fewer people to launch weather balloons. One forecast balloon a day instead of two. The afternoon will have to stop doing weather.”

sources.title: NOAA cuts weather balloon launches, citing staff shortages
sources.qualification: Reporting of a temporary reduction beginning March 20, 2025; not a claim that the reduced schedule remains in effect.

setup.en: At a North Platte grocery bench, a school bus driver recalls the private-school funding vote.

text.en: In November 2024, Nebraska voters repealed the legislature’s provision directing $10 million annually to scholarships for privately operated schools.

comment.en: “The legislature gave private-school scholarships public money. Nebraska voters repealed it. Turns out school choice includes choosing where the state keeps its wallet.”

sources.title: Nebraska Secretary of State: 2024 General Election Canvass
sources.qualification: Certified result for Referendum 435; concerns the specific appropriation repealed, not every subsequent school-choice initiative.

setup.en: At a North Platte diner, a rail worker talks while a freight train passes outside.

text.en: In December 2022, Congress and President Biden imposed a national freight-rail contract to block a strike, including at Union Pacific, which operates North Platte’s rail yard.

comment.en: “Biden and Congress blocked the rail strike. We were essential enough to keep working, just not essential enough to choose when we stopped.”

sources.title: AP: Rail Workers Gain Sick Leave After Imposed Contract
sources.qualification: Reports the prior December imposition and subsequent leave gains; the joke addresses lost strike leverage, not a claim no rail worker later gained sick leave.

sources.title: Union Pacific: Train Types and Hump Yards
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

setup.en: Outside an Oklahoma City grocery, a pantry volunteer unloads some donated food.

text.en: In April 2025, the Regional Food Bank of Oklahoma warned that Trump-administration cancellation of federal local-food purchasing funds would reduce its ability to meet growing demand.

comment.en: “Trump’s USDA canceled local-food funding. Now the pantry asks neighbors to fill the gap. Small government comes with a surprisingly large grocery list.”

sources.title: Federal cuts may soon begin to affect local food banks
sources.qualification: Regional Food Bank of Oklahoma warning about the canceled LFPA program; projected capacity effects are not presented as measured losses.

setup.en: At an Oklahoma City café patio, a school custodian describes the state’s Bible purchase.

text.en: In November 2024, Ryan Walters’ Oklahoma education department said it ordered 500 Trump-endorsed Bibles for classrooms, costing about $25,000.

comment.en: “Walters bought Trump-endorsed Bibles for classrooms. I buy my own work gloves. Apparently public funding depends on whose hands have been on the product.”

sources.title: AP: Oklahoma Superintendent Announces Religious Department and Bible Purchase
sources.qualification: Department’s announced order, not a claim that every classroom received a Bible or that every later purchase proceeded.

setup.en: At an Oklahoma City bus stop, a cafeteria worker talks about private-school tax credits.

text.en: Oklahoma’s official 2025–26 parental-choice tax-credit report allowed up to $250 million in credits for eligible private-school tuition and fees.

comment.en: “Oklahoma authorized a quarter-billion in private-school credits. My school fundraiser still needs baked goods. Can I file these brownies as an educational institution?”

sources.title: Oklahoma Tax Commission: Parental Choice Tax Credit Report
sources.qualification: Authorized annual cap, not a claim the entire amount was spent or that every household qualifies.

setup.en: At an Omaha medical-campus bus stop, a cleaner discusses the proposed research-cost cap.

text.en: In February 2025, Omaha’s UNMC warned that Trump’s proposed NIH research-cost cap threatened expenses including laboratory infrastructure, utilities and cybersecurity.

comment.en: “Trump’s NIH cap treats the light bill as expendable overhead. Fine. Let the next medical breakthrough develop a natural immunity to darkness.”

sources.title: UNMC statement on NIH indirect cost guidance
sources.qualification: University warning about announced NIH guidance; does not claim the proposed cap ultimately took effect or specific layoffs occurred.

setup.en: At an Omaha riverside rest, a plumber talks while you rinse mud from your shoes.

text.en: Before Omaha’s sewer-overflow control program, an average year sent about 3.7 billion gallons of sewage mixed with stormwater into the Missouri River and Papillion Creek.

comment.en: “The city tackles sewage overflows. Taxes or sewage: every household contributes something. I prefer the one with a receipt.”

sources.title: About the Program: Clean Solutions for Omaha
sources.qualification: City wastewater program account; 3.7 billion gallons is the estimated average annual overflow before the program, not a current annual total.

setup.en: At an Omaha sandwich shop’s public bench, a clerk counts coworkers on their fingers.

text.en: Nebraska’s paid-sick-time mandate took effect October 1, 2025, for employers with at least eleven employees. Smaller employers are not required by that mandate to provide it.

comment.en: “Nebraska requires paid sick leave at workplaces with eleven employees. We have ten. My flu is waiting for an eleventh opinion.”

sources.title: Nebraska Department of Labor: Paid Sick Time Effective October 1
sources.qualification: The mandate covers employers with at least eleven employees; accrual and worker eligibility conditions remain.

setup.en: At a Phoenix shaded food stop, a care worker discusses Arizona’s fight for federal money.

text.en: In August 2025, Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said lawsuits against Trump-administration actions had protected about $1.5 billion in federal funds for state programs.

comment.en: “Mayes says lawsuits protected a billion and a half in federal funds. Washington has added a new grant requirement: bring your own attorney general.”

sources.title: Attorney General Mayes Safeguards $1.5 Billion in Federal Funds for Arizona in Lawsuits Against Trump Administration
sources.qualification: Attorney general’s own accounting of statewide funds protected while lawsuits continued; not a final judgment in every case or a Phoenix-only total.

title.en: A Timesheet for Your Blood Pressure

setup.en: At a Phoenix laundromat, a cleaner checks a work schedule while your clothes dry.

text.en: Under Trump’s 2025 law, certain Arizona Medicaid expansion adults face new work or qualifying-activity requirements beginning January 2027. Exemptions apply; the requirements are not universal.

comment.en: “Trump’s law adds Medicaid work checks in 2027. I already clean for a living. Now my health insurance wants a second copy of the floor.”

sources.title: AHCCCS: Federal H.R.1 Changes
sources.qualification: Future January 2027 requirements for certain expansion adults; approved activities, earnings alternatives and exemptions matter.

setup.en: At a Phoenix bus stop, a delivery worker shifts with the narrow shadow of a pole.

text.en: Phoenix’s November 2024 shade plan committed to at least 27,000 trees over five years, while acknowledging that projected planting would still leave unmet shade needs.

comment.en: “The city promised thousands of trees over five years. My bus arrives in twenty minutes. Can the shade plan start with this square foot?”

sources.title: Shade Phoenix: An Action Plan for Trees and Built Shade
sources.qualification: Council draft plan states a five-year commitment to at least 27,000 trees and says projected planting remains insufficient; a target, not completed planting.

setup.en: At a Pittsburgh campus food truck, a lab technician joins you at a standing table.

text.en: At a June 11, 2025 town hall, Pitt reported that federal agencies under Trump had terminated 91 research awards, representing a $42 million loss.

comment.en: “Trump’s agencies canceled ninety-one Pitt awards. The researchers still have questions. Washington has funded the answer: we cannot afford to find out.”

sources.title: Timeline: First half of 2026 brings more research cuts to Pitt
sources.qualification: Updated local reporting; this package uses the explicitly dated June 11, 2025 entry, not the current cumulative grant total.

setup.en: At a Pittsburgh diner exit, an off-duty server pockets a work schedule.

text.en: Pittsburgh’s paid-sick-time expansion took effect January 1, 2026, allowing covered workers at employers with at least fifteen employees to accrue up to 72 hours annually.

comment.en: “Pittsburgh expanded paid sick time. Finally, the cough can stay home instead of explaining the specials. The germs are furious about government interference.”

sources.title: City of Pittsburgh: Paid Sick Days Act
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Paid Sick Days Act Guidelines
sources.qualification: Accrual cap and eligibility requirements, not an immediate bank of 72 hours for every worker.

setup.en: At a Pittsburgh overlook, a window cleaner rests beside your food bag.

text.en: Pittsburgh adopted a smoke-control ordinance and created a Bureau of Smoke Prevention in 1941, giving local government a formal role in controlling industrial smoke.

comment.en: “Pittsburgh had to pass a law to get smoke out of the air. Industry had been providing free samples directly into everybody’s lungs.”

sources.title: Guide to the Allegheny County Health Department, Bureau of Air Pollution Control Records, 1941–1978
sources.qualification: University archival finding aid verified through indexed text; direct page rejected retrieval. Supports the 1941 ordinance and bureau.

setup.en: At a Rapid City campground table, a cleaner compares park dates with your route.

text.en: Nearby Badlands National Park’s 2026 fee-free schedule includes June 14, described as Flag Day and President Trump’s birthday, for US citizens and residents.

comment.en: “Trump made his birthday a free park day. I tried celebrating mine at the gate. Apparently the birthday discount requires executive experience.”

sources.title: Badlands National Park: Fees & Passes
sources.qualification: Official 2026 schedule checked September 13; free entrance days apply to US citizens and residents and may exclude other fees.

setup.en: Stopping to check your map, you meet a Rapid City cleaner rolling a bin along a vacation rental’s wide driveway.

text.en: Rapid City’s council approved vacation-rental rules in December 2025 requiring two off-street parking spaces.

comment.en: “Council wants two parking spaces for a vacation rental. The guests get bunk beds. Their trucks each get a private suite.”

sources.title: Rapid City council votes to regulate vacation home rentals
sources.qualification: Supports the two-space requirement under the new vacation-rental rules. No assertion about every existing property’s status or a city requirement that guests use bunk beds.

title.en: The Book Cannot Cross the State

setup.en: Outside a Rapid City library, a hotel worker compares reading plans with you.

text.en: In May 2025, South Dakota’s state library suspended interlibrary loans amid Trump-administration disruption of federal library grants, limiting access to books held elsewhere.

comment.en: “Trump’s library cuts halted the state loan program. The book exists, just somewhere else. We have invented a library card that needs a fuel budget.”

sources.title: AP: Libraries Cut Services After Trump Targets IMLS
sources.qualification: Dated interlibrary-loan suspension; court orders and later restoration are not summarized as a current blanket closure.

setup.en: At a Reno campus picnic table, a technician shifts a lunch cooler into the shade.

text.en: In February 2025, the University of Nevada, Reno said Trump’s announced research-cost cap threatened over $4 million annually; a court had temporarily blocked it.

comment.en: “Trump proposed capping the money that keeps labs running. Courts paused it. My lunch now has two protections: this cooler and the separation of powers.”

sources.title: Update on NIH Funding
sources.qualification: University estimate of more than $4 million annually at risk; the same notice reported a temporary court order blocking implementation.

setup.en: At a Reno laundromat, a retired cleaner compares a rental renewal with your travel budget.

text.en: Governor Joe Lombardo vetoed Nevada’s AB280 in June 2025, rejecting fee protections and a temporary 5% rent-increase cap for certain tenants, citing affordability concerns.

comment.en: “Lombardo vetoed a rent cap because it could hurt affordability. Good news: my rent can rise freely to protect me from expensive housing.”

sources.title: Governor Lombardo: AB280 Veto Message
sources.qualification: Failed bill with targeted tenant coverage; the governor’s predicted affordability effects are his stated rationale, not proven results.

setup.en: At a Reno riverside bench, a maintenance worker describes the federal diversion downstream.

text.en: The federal Derby Dam, completed near Reno in 1905, diverted Truckee River water for irrigation, reducing flows to Pyramid Lake and harming fish important to the Paiute Tribe.

comment.en: “Washington sent Truckee water toward its irrigation project. Pyramid Lake and Paiute fish got less. Federal generosity is easiest when somebody else owns the bucket.”

sources.title: Bureau of Reclamation: Newlands Project
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

sources.title: Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe: Fishing and Water History
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

title.en: The Cure Has an Overhead Problem

setup.en: At a Salt Lake City campus café patio, a lab cleaner waits for a bus.

text.en: In 2025, University of Utah research leaders estimated that Trump’s proposed NIH reimbursement reduction would cut university research revenue by about $45 million.

comment.en: “Trump’s NIH proposal threatened forty-five million in research revenue. Apparently the cure should cover its own rent. Has anyone tried asking the disease for a deposit?”

sources.title: U research leaders: Keep doing the science
sources.qualification: University account verified through indexed text; $45 million was the estimated impact of a proposed NIH reduction, not a realized loss.

setup.en: At a downtown Salt Lake City transit stop, a cleaner helps you locate the Free Fare Zone.

text.en: UTA charges no fare for TRAX and fixed-route bus trips that both start and end inside downtown Salt Lake City’s designated Free Fare Zone.

comment.en: “UTA makes these downtown trips free. Cross the zone boundary and fares return. Even government kindness has learned to read a property map.”

sources.title: UTA Free Fare Zone
sources.qualification: Operator rules checked September 2026; both boarding and exiting must occur within the zone, and the rule does not make all regional transit free.

setup.en: Near Salt Lake City Hall, a seamstress pauses while you rest on the steps.

text.en: In May 2025, Salt Lake City adopted new official Pride, transgender and Juneteenth-themed city flags after Utah restricted which flags government buildings could display.

comment.en: “Utah tried banning unofficial flags. The city made Pride flags official. The rainbow is still here; it just had to pass a municipal background check.”

sources.title: Salt Lake City: Four Official City Flags
sources.qualification: Primary source; dated or historical action only.

sources.title: AP: Salt Lake City and Boise Adopt Official Pride Flags
sources.qualification: Dated response to the 2025 law; not a claim about every subsequent legislative change.

setup.en: At a San Antonio playground bench, a school aide discusses the federal funding freeze.

text.en: During Trump’s January 2025 federal funding-freeze confusion, San Antonio ISD said affected programs would continue while it awaited state and federal guidance.

comment.en: “Trump froze funding; the district kept programs running while waiting for instructions. The children also kept being children. Terrible failure to coordinate with Washington.”

sources.title: Will Trump’s federal funding freeze impact San Antonio Head Start programs?
sources.qualification: Local report says SAISD expected operations to continue and was awaiting guidance; this is uncertainty, not a documented program closure.

title.en: The Tuition Has a State Escort

setup.en: At a San Antonio grocery queue, a bus driver adds pencils to a small food purchase.

text.en: Governor Abbott signed Texas’s education savings-account program in 2025, with $1 billion in initial state funding for eligible private-education expenses.

comment.en: “Abbott gave private-school accounts a billion-dollar launch. My child’s classroom still requests pencils. I should have sent the supply list to a lobbyist.”

sources.title: Texas Education Freedom Accounts
sources.qualification: State allocation and program purpose; no claim that a specific school’s pencil budget was directly transferred to the program.

setup.en: At a San Antonio garage, a mechanic taps a registration receipt while you ask about the new rules.

text.en: Texas ended most noncommercial vehicle safety inspections in January 2025 but kept a $7.50 replacement fee; emissions and commercial inspection requirements remain.

comment.en: “They scrapped most safety inspections and kept the fee. The car stays outside. Open your wallet and say ‘ah.’”

sources.title: Texas DPS: Vehicle Safety Inspection Changes Take Effect January 2025
sources.qualification: Most noncommercial safety inspections ended; applicable emissions and commercial rules remain. The fee is not represented as the entire vehicle-registration bill.

setup.en: At a Sioux Falls food pantry’s public bench, a delivery worker talks about the funding gap.

text.en: In July 2025, Feeding South Dakota asked state lawmakers for $3 million after Trump-era federal cuts reduced its food supply across the state.

comment.en: “Federal cuts left Feeding South Dakota asking legislators for three million. Hunger now needs a committee hearing. It has prepared some very brief stomach remarks.”

sources.title: Feeding South Dakota asks South Dakota lawmakers for $3M due to federal cuts
sources.qualification: Statewide food-bank account, discussed in Sioux Falls; the $3 million was a request, not an awarded grant or a Sioux Falls-only loss.
